domains.summary: The Users & KYC domain has a substantial "just-wire" backbone already built (list end users, user detail aggregate, devices, tier/status/pin-reset/device-revoke/sim-swap mutations, KYC queue + submission + approve/reject), fully covered by contracts, lib/api clients (users.ts, kyc.ts) AND TanStack hooks — but all three FE screens still render module-level mock consts and call none of it. So the largest bucket is "just-wire" (replace mock with the existing hooks). A second bucket is real functionality the design mock shows that has NO backend at all ("mock-only-needs-backend"): manual credit (engine-brokered admin credit), per-user limits/velocity view, add-note/admin-action timeline, active auth-sessions + revoke-all/revoke-single (the backend models devices, not sessions), full-PII reveal (only last-4 is ever exposed — a deliberate invariant, so this is a design/security conflict not a build item), KYC "request more info", KYC document images + name-enquiry surfacing, resend-verification, view-as/impersonate, CSV export, and bulk tag/message. A few backend capabilities are built but not surfaced by these screens ("backend-only-not-surfaced"): per-user transactions filter (AdminTxnSearchQuery.userId), the conversation/chat log (exists but not scoped to a user), the recentLedger array in the detail aggregate, and the beneficiary cooling-off override. NOTE: admin-users.controller.ts manages admin CONSOLE accounts (/admin/admins), NOT platform end users — end users are admin-end-users.controller.ts (/admin/users); do not confuse them. Recommended phasing: Phase 1 = wire the ~13 existing endpoints into the three screens; Phase 2 = build the read-only gaps (limits/velocity, sessions, timeline, chat-for-user, KYC docs/name-enquiry, request-info); Phase 3 = decide on money-adjacent + PII items (manual credit via the engine, full-PII reveal policy) which touch invariants §3.1/§3.4 and need product/compliance sign-off.

items.feature: Users list (directory table: customer, KYC, tier, country, balance, risk, last-active)
items.detail: users-page.tsx renders a 28-row module const USERS and filters client-side. Endpoint+contract+client+hook all exist. Wire useEndUsers(query) and map AdminEndUserListItem (id,email,status,kycStatus,kycTier,simSwapFlagged,createdAt). Field mismatches to resolve: mock shows NGN balance, country, tier label, last-active, and per-user risk flags (simSwap/sanctions/velocity) — the list item ONLY provides simSwapFlagged, no balance/country/last-active/tier-in-list/sanctions/velocity flags, so those columns either need list-response enrichment (backend) or must be dropped. Server filters are query/status/kycTier only (no country, no risk-chip, no free-text-on-phone).

items.feature: Users list search + filters (KYC status, tier, country, risk chips) + pagination
items.detail: Search + KYC + tier filters map to query/status/kycTier. GAPS: country filter and the three risk chips (simSwap/sanctions/velocity) have no query params (only status/kycTier supported); simSwap is only a boolean on the row, sanctions/velocity are not modeled at all. Pagination differs: FE mock is offset (10/page); backend is keyset cursor (nextCursor) — the FE Pagination primitive needs to move to cursor or the query needs offset support. Country + sanctions/velocity filters are mock-only-needs-backend sub-parts.

items.feature: Users list — Export CSV (header + bulk bar)
items.detail: Mock 'Export CSV' just pushes a toast. No /admin/users/export endpoint exists anywhere. Needs a backend streaming/paginated CSV export (respecting the same filters + PII minimization) plus a client. Money-safe (read-only) but must audit the export.

items.feature: Users list — bulk actions (Tag, Message) on selected rows
items.detail: Bulk-bar Tag and Message only emit toasts. No user-tagging model or bulk-messaging/notification-to-end-users endpoint exists in the admin module. Tag needs a tags table + endpoints; Message needs a bulk outbound comms path (ties into notifications module). Both are net-new backend.

items.feature: User detail — Profile tab (contact & locale)
items.detail: user-detail.tsx renders const CU (Amara Okeke) and ignores the route id (void _props). Wire useEndUserDetail(id). GAP: AdminEndUserDetail provides id,email,status,kycStatus,kycTier,simSwapDetectedAt,createdAt only — the mock's phone, country, locale, marketing-consent, avatar hue, initials are NOT in the contract, so Contact&locale panel is partly unbacked (needs detail enrichment or dropping those rows).

items.feature: User detail — Profile Admin-action timeline + Add note
items.detail: Timeline is a local useState list; Add note prepends a row in-memory. No per-user note/timeline model or endpoint exists (audit log exists but is chain-integrity events keyed by subject, not a user-facing notes feed with free-text). Needs an admin-note entity + POST /admin/users/:id/notes + a per-user timeline read (could derive partly from the audit trail filtered by subject User:<id>).

items.feature: User detail — KYC tab: identity documents (NIN/BVN last-4, ID front, selfie)
items.detail: KycSubmissionDetail provides ninLast4,bvnLast4,idDocumentType,livenessResult,firstName,lastName,dateOfBirth,status,tier,rejectionReason — enough to wire the masked NIN/BVN and status. GAPS: ID_FRONT.jpg and SELFIE.jpg image placeholders have NO backing field (no document image URLs in the contract or service) — mock-only-needs-backend sub-part (needs signed-URL surfacing of the KYC document store).

items.feature: User detail — KYC tab: full NIN/BVN reveal (Reveal → step-up → decrypted PII banner, auto-remask)
items.detail: The design's marquee PII-reveal flow (reveal full NIN/BVN, 'access is logged', auto-remask 20s) has NO endpoint — the backend DELIBERATELY only ever exposes last-4 (AdminKycReviewService.last4 + comments 'the full NIN/BVN never leaves the backend'). This is a direct CONFLICT with invariant-style PII minimization. Building it means a new audited decrypt endpoint (step-up gated, rate-limited, logged) that contradicts the current 'never leaves backend' stance — needs explicit compliance/product decision before any build, not a routine gap.

items.feature: User detail — KYC tab: name-enquiry match panel
items.detail: Mock shows a bank name-enquiry 'Match · <name>' result. KycSubmissionDetail has no name-enquiry field (livenessResult exists, but not the bank account-holder name-match result). Needs a field on the submission detail (the name-enquiry data is produced elsewhere in the KYC/beneficiary flow — surface it here).

items.feature: User detail — KYC tab: Approve (maker-checker) / Request info / Reject
items.detail: Approve→ wire useApproveKyc({tier}); Reject→ wire useRejectKyc({reason}) via the ReasonModal text. Both are step-up gated (403 ADMIN_STEP_UP_REQUIRED → useStepUpRetry). GAPS: (1) 'Request info' (needs_info) has NO endpoint — approve/reject only; needs a POST /admin/kyc/:userId/request-info. (2) The 'maker-checker' second-approver flow the design shows is not represented in the approve endpoint (single-call approve) — either drop the maker-checker UI or build a two-phase approval. Wiring approve/reject = just-wire; request-info + maker-checker = mock-only-needs-backend.

items.feature: User detail — Devices tab (list bound devices, SIM-swap badge, Unbind)
items.detail: Devices are also embedded in the detail aggregate. Wire the list; 'Unbind' → useRevokeDevice (step-up). AdminEndUserDevice has id,trustState,isPinned,lastUsedAt,boundAt — the mock's device name/fingerprint/OS and the per-device 'SIM-SWAP 2d ago' badge are NOT in the contract (only simSwapDetectedAt at the user level). Device name/fp/os = needs contract+detail enrichment; simSwapReverify endpoint exists but the per-device SIM-swap badge is user-level.

items.feature: User detail — SIM-swap reverify trigger
items.detail: Full backend endpoint + client + hook exist, but NO design screen exposes a 'trigger sim-swap reverify' action — the Devices tab only shows a passive SIM-SWAP badge and an Unbind button. Either add a 'Force re-verify (SIM-swap)' action button in the Devices/Security tab, or treat as intentional (the badge is informational). Recommend surfacing it near the SIM-swap badge.

items.feature: User detail — Security tab: active sessions (list, Revoke, Revoke all)
items.detail: Mock lists end-user auth SESSIONS (UA, IP, when) with Revoke + Revoke-all. The backend models DEVICES (bind/revoke) but has NO end-user auth-session read or revoke in the admin module (loadUserWithKycAndDevices has no session concept). Note: admin.ts listSessions/revokeSession are the ADMIN's OWN console sessions, not the end user's. Needs new endpoints: GET /admin/users/:id/sessions, DELETE .../:sessionId, POST .../sessions/revoke-all.

items.feature: User detail — Security tab: PIN status / lockouts / 2FA + Reset PIN directive
items.detail: The Reset-PIN action is a just-wire (forcePinReset endpoint+client+hook exist, step-up gated). BUT the READ side (PIN status 'Set · last set 12d ago', failed-PIN lockouts, OTP lockouts, 2FA enrolled) is entirely mock — no field on AdminEndUserDetail carries PIN-set time, lockout counts, or 2FA state. So the reset button = just-wire; the security-status panel = mock-only-needs-backend (needs detail enrichment).

items.feature: User detail — Wallets & balances tab (asset cards + on-chain deposit addresses)
items.detail: balances[] exists in the detail aggregate — wire the USDT/TRX/total cards from it (NGN total needs FX conversion, which the detail does not provide — pricing/FX join needed). GAP: the 'on-chain deposit addresses' list (child addresses per asset) is NOT in the contract — no address field on the balance or detail. Cards = just-wire; deposit-address list = mock-only-needs-backend (surface child addresses from the wallets module).

items.feature: User detail — Wallets tab: Manual credit (reason→step-up→engine→maker-checker)
items.detail: The design's most sensitive action: an engine-brokered manual credit showing an effect table + double-entry ledger (treasury:USDT DR / user:USDT CR) + idempotency key + maker-checker. NO manual-credit endpoint exists anywhere (grep for manual.?credit across api/src returns nothing). This MOVES MONEY, so per §3.1 it must be built as a proposal→deterministic-engine execution (idempotency, maker-checker, audit), not a direct write. High-effort, money-path — needs the engine to expose an admin manual-credit proposal path. Product/compliance sign-off required.

items.feature: User detail — Beneficiaries tab (list + Remove)
items.detail: The user-detail aggregate already includes beneficiaries[], and a per-user-scoped list (listBeneficiaries(userId)) exists via useAdminBeneficiaries(userId). Wire either. GAP: the mock 'Remove' action has NO backend — admin-beneficiaries.controller.ts exposes ONLY cooling-off-override (POST), no DELETE. Removing an end-user beneficiary from admin needs a new endpoint. List = just-wire; Remove = mock-only-needs-backend.

items.feature: User detail — Transactions tab (recent txns list, click → tx detail)
items.detail: Two ways to wire: the detail aggregate's recentTransactions[10], or the transactions list filtered by userId (AdminTxnSearchQuery.userId exists). GAP: AdminEndUserTxn lacks the USDT/NGN amount columns the mock shows (id,type,status,createdAt only); AdminTxnListItem may carry amounts — prefer listTransactions({userId}) for the amount columns. Row click → /transactions/:id (that detail route is a separate domain but exists).

items.feature: User detail — Chat history tab (read-only transcript with intent→proposal chips)
items.feApiClient: listConversations / getConversation (agent.ts) — NOT scoped to a user
items.detail: The conversation-log backend EXISTS (messages, per-message intent {action,confidence}, replies) and ConversationLogItem/Detail carry userId — so the data is available. GAP: the list endpoint has NO userId filter param (AdminPaginationQueryDto only), so surfacing a single user's chat needs either a userId query param added to listConversations OR resolving the user's conversation id first. The user-detail Chat tab renders mock. Classify as backend-mostly-present but needs a per-user filter + FE wiring.

items.feature: User detail — Limits tab (effective per-tier caps + overrides + live velocity usage)
items.detail: Mock shows effective limits (daily/weekly/per-tx/tx-count caps) with an OVERRIDE badge and live velocity bars (daily-send used, tx count 24h, swap volume 24h). NO admin endpoint returns per-user effective limits or current velocity usage, and no per-user limit-override write exists. Tier limits live in DB-admin config (§7) but are not surfaced per user with the user's live velocity counters. Needs GET /admin/users/:id/limits (effective caps + velocity) and optionally a per-user override write. Read-only velocity is money-adjacent but non-mutating.

items.feature: User detail — header: Tier override (maker-checker) + Force re-KYC
items.detail: 'Override tier' → wire useAdjustTier({tier}) (step-up gated). GAPS: (1) the design's maker-checker (second approver) is not in the single-call PATCH — drop the maker-checker UI or build two-phase. (2) 'Force re-KYC' has NO dedicated endpoint (there's sim-swap-reverify and status change, but not a force-re-KYC that resets kycStatus to pending) — mock-only-needs-backend. Tier change = just-wire; force-re-KYC + maker-checker = needs backend.

items.feature: User detail — header: Freeze / Unfreeze account
items.detail: The mock 'Freeze' (reason→step-up) maps to setStatus('suspended'); unfreeze = setStatus('active'). Endpoint+client+hook exist, step-up gated. Straight wire — map the Freeze button + FROZEN badge to status==='suspended'/'deactivated'. The mock's 'frozen' boolean should be derived from status.

items.feature: User detail — header: Add note / Resend verification / View as
items.detail: Three header actions with no backend: 'Add note' (same missing notes model as the Profile timeline), 'Resend' verification link (no resend endpoint in admin — ties to notifications/identity), and 'View as' (impersonation — no impersonate endpoint; a high-risk feature that likely should NOT exist for a custodial fintech admin without a strict audited read-only session model). Recommend: build Add-note + Resend; explicitly defer/decline View-as pending security review.

items.feature: KYC review queue page (status tabs pending/needs_info/approved/rejected + queue table)
items.detail: kyc-review-page.tsx re-seeds the 28-user mock and buckets by status client-side. GAP: the backend queue (listUsersPendingKycReview) returns ONLY pending-review users — it is NOT a 4-tab (pending/needs_info/approved/rejected) queryable queue; there is no status filter param on GET /admin/kyc/queue. So the pending tab = just-wire; the needs_info/approved/rejected tabs need a status filter added to the queue endpoint (mock-only-needs-backend sub-part). Also the mock's SLA age and Assignee columns have NO backing fields (KycQueueItem has no SLA/assignee) — needs enrichment. Row click → /users/:id?tab=kyc already aligns with the wired KYC tab.

domains.summary: All three web-admin screens (transactions-page, transaction-detail, ledger-page) are pure design reproductions rendering module-level mock consts — none import a query hook or api client. A real read-only oversight + engine-brokered triage backend already exists (AdminTransactionsController, AdminTxnTriageController, AdminLedgerController) with matching contracts (admin-txn, txn-action, admin-ledger) and lib/api clients (transactions.ts, ledger.ts) plus TanStack hooks (useTransactions, useTransactionDetail, useLedgerHistory, useMarkFailed, useRetrySettlement, useVerifyLedger). So the transactions list, detail, and the two money-path actions (retry, mark-failed) are largely "just-wire". BUT three real backend gaps exist: (1) the txn-list contract returns NO amount/asset/idempotency-key/user-name, so the FE list's amount, asset, idempotency-key and user columns + the free-text search over hash/ref/idem + the per-view count pills have no backend to feed them; (2) the Ledger page browses ALL accounts by account-TYPE prefix + currency, but GET /admin/ledger requires a full (accountType, accountId, currency) triple and there is no global cross-account list, no CSV export, and no sequence-integrity endpoint; (3) the detail page's "Resend receipt" and per-transaction "Re-run recon" action buttons have no admin endpoint (wallet-level reconcile exists but is user-scoped, not per-transaction). Phase plan: P1 wire list/detail/retry/mark-failed + verify; P2 enrich txn-list DTO (amount/asset/idem/user + free-text search + counts) and build global ledger list + export + integrity; P3 build resend-receipt + per-txn recon.

items.feature: Transactions list — table rows (id, type, user, status, created)
items.detail: FE transactions-page.tsx renders the module-level TXNS[] const (no hook imported). The endpoint + contract + client (listTransactions) + hook (useTransactions) all exist and return {id,userId,type,status,createdAt} keyset-paginated. Wiring: replace TXNS with useTransactions(query); map status via existing StatusPill. Only the base columns (id/type/status/created) map cleanly — amount/asset/user-name/idem columns are separate gaps below.

items.feature: Transactions list — Amount (USDT + NGN) and Asset columns
items.detail: FE list shows per-row USDT amount, asset (USDT/TRX/USDT→TRX) and NGN fiat leg. AdminTxnListItemSchema has ONLY {id,userId,type,status,createdAt} — no amount/asset/fiat. These live in Transaction.metadata (asset, cryptoAmount, fiatAmount, fxRate); the list repo projection does not surface them. Needs: widen AdminTxnListItemSchema + AdminTxnOversightService.toListItem + transaction repo listAll projection to include amount/asset/fiat from metadata.

items.feature: Transactions list — Idempotency-key column (copy-on-click)
items.detail: FE list renders t.idem per row with a copy affordance. idempotencyKey exists on AdminTxnDetail (detail endpoint) but NOT on AdminTxnListItem. Add idempotencyKey to the list-item schema + service mapper + repo projection (the column already exists on the Transaction row, trivial to project).

items.feature: Transactions list — User display name column
items.detail: FE shows a human name ('Amara Okeke'). The list item exposes only userId (uuid). Backend must either join the user's display name/handle into the list projection or the FE must resolve names via a batch user lookup. Simplest: add a userLabel/displayName to AdminTxnListItem via a repo join (User table). Effort M because it crosses into the identity module.

items.feature: Transactions list — view tabs (All / Stuck-Pending / Failed today / Refunds) with count pills
items.detail: The status filter can drive each tab (stuck→settling/pending_settlement, failed→failed, refunds→refunded) so the FILTERING is just-wire, BUT: (a) 'Failed today' needs a from=startOfDay bound (supported via from/to) and (b) the per-tab count PILLS have no backend — there is no aggregate-count endpoint. Note also a status-vocabulary mismatch: FE uses pending_settlement/refunded/quoted/initiated/receive; BE AdminTxnStatus enum is pending/validating/confirmed/settling/completed/failed/rolled_back/cancelled — a mapping layer is required. Counts need a small counts endpoint or a metrics query.

items.feature: Transactions list — free-text search by id / chain-hash / provider-ref / idempotency-key
items.detail: FE search filters TXNS by id.includes / chainHash / flwRef / idem. AdminTxnSearchQuerySchema supports status/type/userId/from/to/cursor/limit but NO free-text 'q'. Needs a search param + repo WHERE across id, onChainTxHash, processorTxRef, idempotencyKey (and metadata refs). Effort M — repo query + contract + service.

items.feature: Transaction detail — itemized parameters (amount, fiat leg, rate, fee, spread, internal margin)
items.detail: FE PARAMS shows Amount(USDT), Fiat leg(NGN), spread-folded Rate, Processing fee, FX spread bps, and an operator-only Internal margin. AdminTxnDetail exposes id/userId/type/status/idempotencyKey/processorTxRef/onChainTxHash/failureReason/timestamps/ledgerLegs/timeline — but NO amount/rate/fee/spread/margin fields. These derive from Transaction.metadata + fxRateSnapshot + config spread; backend must project an economics/itemized block (incl. operator-only margin, gated) onto the detail DTO.

items.feature: Transaction detail — double-entry ledger mini-table (Account/Dir/Amount/Seq)
items.detail: FE LEDGER const mirrors AdminTxnLedgerLeg exactly (accountType/accountId/currency/amount/direction/balanceAfter/postedAt). The detail endpoint already returns ledgerLegs via ledger.listByTransaction. Wire ledgerLegs into the mini-table; FE's 'seq' display can use array index or add sequence (sequence exists on AdminLedgerEntry but AdminTxnLedgerLeg omits it — add sequence to the leg schema if the Seq column must be real, else S).

items.feature: Transaction detail — engine state timeline (stepper)
items.detail: FE TIMELINE is a hardcoded 5-step stepper. AdminTxnDetail.timeline is derived from the txn's non-null timestamps (created/settling/completed/failed) via deriveTimeline. Wire timeline[] into the stepper. Note the BE timeline is coarser (4 lifecycle states, no Quoted/Directive/webhook sub-steps) — acceptable if FE renders what BE provides; richer sub-steps would need a per-txn event log (not present).

items.feature: Transaction detail — provider references (TRON hash + Tronscan link, Flutterwave ref, Blockradar, idempotency)
items.detail: FE REFS shows TRON hash (+Tronscan href), Flutterwave ref, Blockradar id, idempotency. AdminTxnDetail exposes onChainTxHash (→TRON+Tronscan), processorTxRef (→Flutterwave), idempotencyKey. The separate 'Blockradar' ref has no dedicated DTO field (it may live in metadata as blockradar/depositId) — wire the three present fields; the Blockradar row needs a metadata projection or drop it. Mostly just-wire.

items.feature: Transaction detail — webhook history list
items.detail: FE WEBHOOKS shows per-txn webhook events (blockradar.deposit.detected, flutterwave.settlement.pending) with delivered/in-flight tone. There is NO admin endpoint, contract, client, or service exposing a per-transaction webhook/event history. Would require a webhook-event store + a GET /admin/transactions/:id/webhooks projection. Flag as intentional-omission candidate for P3 or drop the panel if no event log is persisted.

items.feature: Transaction detail — Retry settlement action
items.detail: FE 'Retry settlement' opens the step-up→engine modal chain but only advances local state (no request). The endpoint (retry re-enqueues the settlement outbox, moves no money), client (retryTransaction), hook (useRetrySettlement, invalidates txns), and step-up 403 handling all exist. Wire the EngineActionModal onExecute to useRetrySettlement wrapped in useStepUpRetry.

items.feature: Transaction detail — Mark failed action (with refund)
items.detail: FE 'Mark failed' runs reason→step-up→engine locally. Endpoint exists and is engine-brokered (routes through settle{Sell,Send,Swap}RefundAtomic, audited, idempotent, step-up-guarded). Client markTransactionFailed + hook useMarkFailed exist. Wire the ReasonModal reason into AdminTxnMarkFailedRequest and EngineActionModal onExecute → useMarkFailed. Note BE only allows mark-failed on a 'settling' sell/send/swap (rejects others) — FE must surface TxnNotTriageableError as an error branch.

items.feature: Transaction detail — Refund (partial, maker-checker over threshold) action
items.detail: FE 'Refund' opens reason→step-up→engine and, when the partial-refund amount exceeds ₦100,000, adds a maker-checker approval step. There is NO admin refund endpoint/contract/client — mark-failed does a FULL reserve reversal, not an operator-specified PARTIAL refund, and there is NO maker-checker (two-person-approval) workflow anywhere in the admin backend. Needs a new engine-brokered partial-refund directive + a maker-checker approval domain (request/approve/execute) — the largest single gap. Effort L.

items.feature: Transaction detail — Re-run reconciliation (per-transaction) action
items.beEndpoint: none (wallet-level reconcile is user-scoped, not per-txn)
items.detail: FE 'Re-run recon' opens a step-up→engine flow scoped to THIS transaction. There is NO per-transaction recon endpoint. POST /admin/wallets/reconcile exists but takes a userId and reconciles on-chain-vs-ledger deposits for a whole user — a different action, not per-txn settlement recon. Either build a per-txn recon endpoint (re-run settlement reconciliation for one txn) or repoint the FE button at the existing retry (outbox re-enqueue) if semantics match. Effort M.

items.feature: Transaction detail — Resend receipt action
items.detail: FE 'Resend receipt' is a no-op toast ('Receipt re-sent'). No admin endpoint/contract/client for resending a transaction receipt/statement to the customer. A statement/receipt generator exists in the transactions module (pdf-statement.generator, statement-token.service) but is not exposed as an admin action. Needs a POST /admin/transactions/:id/resend-receipt wired to notifications + statement services.

items.feature: Ledger page — double-entry table (Seq/Account/Dir/Amount/Running/Source) browsing ALL accounts
items.detail: FE ledger-page.tsx browses ledger legs across ALL accounts, filtered only by account-TYPE prefix (user/treasury/revenue/float) + currency, with a per-currency running balance and Source→txn links. But GET /admin/ledger REQUIRES a full (accountType, accountId, currency) triple (AdminLedgerHistoryQueryDto: all three .min(1)) — it cannot serve a global cross-account browse, and there is no keyset pagination on it. Needs a NEW global ledger-list endpoint (filter by accountType-prefix + currency, cursor-paginated, newest-first) returning AdminLedgerEntry[] (which already carries sequence + running balanceAfter). Effort L (new repo query + contract + client + hook).

items.feature: Ledger page — Export (CSV)
items.detail: FE Export button fires a toast stand-in ('Exporting ledger to CSV…'). No admin ledger-export endpoint/contract/client exists. Needs a GET /admin/ledger/export (streamed CSV, respecting the same account/currency filters). Effort M.

items.feature: Ledger page — Sequence integrity indicator (header 'Sequence integrity OK' pill)
items.detail: FE shows a static global 'Sequence integrity OK' pill. The existing verify endpoint checks ONE transaction's legs net to zero — it is NOT a global per-(account,currency) sequence-continuity check. There is no endpoint that validates the ledger's global sequence integrity (no gaps/reorders across accounts). Either build a global integrity/sequence-continuity endpoint or scope the pill to the currently viewed account. Effort M.

items.feature: Ledger page — Source → transaction detail navigation
items.detail: FE links each tx-sourced row to /transactions/[id]. AdminLedgerEntry already carries transactionId, so once the ledger list is wired the Source link maps directly. Pure client wiring on top of the ledger-list gap above; non-tx sources (e.g. sweeps) have no txn link — the FE already handles that null case.

items.feature: Per-transaction ledger integrity verify (backend capability)
items.detail: A per-transaction integrity check (re-sum legs, per-currency net-to-zero) exists end-to-end: endpoint, contract (AdminLedgerIntegrityResult), client (verifyLedger), hook (useVerifyLedger). No design screen surfaces a per-txn 'verify integrity' button — the txn-detail page has no such action and the ledger page's integrity pill is global-not-per-txn. Surface it as a button on the transaction-detail ledger panel (S), or note as intentional omission if the global integrity pill is deemed sufficient.

domains.summary: Across the four Compliance & Audit repro screens (Sanctions, AML/risk, Blocked list, Audit log), the backend is far more complete than the screens admit: a full compliance console (flagged-events queue+disposition, AML-rule CRUD, sanctions screening-run history, Travel-Rule capture, SAR/STR draft/submit) and a hash-chained audit log (list + chain-verify) all exist as real controllers + contracts + web-admin api-clients + TanStack hooks — yet every screen renders module-level mock consts and never calls a hook. So the bulk of the work is JUST-WIRE (swap consts for the existing hooks, reconcile the design's shapes to the real DTOs). Three genuine backend gaps: (1) the Sanctions page's per-match Clear/Escalate/Block disposition and the numeric match "score"/name+list card shape are NOT what the read-only SanctionsRecord endpoint returns — that endpoint is immutable history with only verdict clear/hit/inconclusive and no disposition mutation, so the disposition actions must be re-homed onto compliance-event disposition or a new sanctions-disposition endpoint must be built; (2) the Sanctions "Ongoing monitoring" toggles have no backend/contract at all; (3) the Audit "Export CSV" button has no export endpoint. The Blocked-list screen is a special case: its store is the compliance.sanctionsDenylist AppSetting (a string[]) edited via the existing PATCH /admin/settings/:key route + UpdateSettingRequestSchema contract — the endpoint and contract exist, but web-admin has NO settings api-client or read hook at all (only getPublicConfig), so both read and Add/Remove need a thin client built. Also unsurfaced by any screen: compliance-event detail drill-in, event severity/status filters, SAR/STR report list + submit, AML-rule create (only edit is mocked), and audit filters (actor/action/date) + cursor pagination (design paginates client-side over 6 mock rows).

items.feature: Audit log — list/table (Actor+role · Action chip · Target · Before→after · Reason · Time)
items.detail: AuditPage renders the verbatim `AUDIT` mock const (6 rows) with client-side search+pagination. A complete BE read exists: GET /admin/audit (AdminAuditController.list) → AuditLogListResponseSchema, with web-admin client `listAudit` and hook `useAudit(query)` already built. Wire: replace the const + local filter with useAudit, map the search box onto the DTO's subject/action filters (server-side) or keep client filter, and switch the client-slice Pagination to the DTO's nextCursor keyset. Shape reconciliation: design's actor is a display name + separate role; contract exposes flat `actor` string + nullable actorAdminId/actorUserId (role not carried → derive/label or extend DTO). before/after are z.unknown() (design assumes strings). Design row carries `ip` but the table never displays it; contract has no ip field — no action unless an IP column is wanted.

items.feature: Audit log — hash-chain verified indicator
items.detail: AuditPage shows a STATIC green 'Hash-chain verified' pill (hardcoded markup, never verified). BE POST /admin/audit/verify (AdminAuditController.verify → AuditChainVerifyResponseSchema {ok, checked, brokenAt}) exists with client `verifyAuditChain` and hook `useVerifyAuditChain`. Wire the pill to the verify result: ok→verified badge, else a broken-at banner. Note there is no permanent 'last-verified' GET — the pill would reflect an on-demand verify (design intent is a passive badge, so consider running verify on mount or adding a lightweight GET).

items.feature: Audit log — Export (CSV)
items.detail: The Export button only fires pushToast('Exporting audit log to CSV…'). No export endpoint exists (grep of admin presentation shows no /audit/export, no csv). Needs BE: a streaming GET /admin/audit/export (respecting the same filters, permissioned, likely capped/async for large ranges) + a contract for the request filters + FE client + download wiring. A client-side CSV of only the fetched page would contradict 'export the audit log' (full, filtered), so flag as backend work.

items.feature: AML/risk — Risk rules list + edit threshold (maker-checker)
items.detail: AmlPage renders the `RISK_RULES` const (name/desc/threshold as a display string) and the edit pencil opens a MakerCheckerModal that no-ops. Full BE CRUD exists: GET /admin/compliance/aml-rules (listAmlRules), PATCH /admin/compliance/aml-rules/:id (updateAmlRule, step-up-gated) → AmlRuleSchema, with clients listAmlRules/updateAmlRule and hooks useAmlRules/useUpdateAmlRule. Wire: replace const with useAmlRules and make the edit modal submit a real AmlRuleUpdateRequest. Shape gap: design shows a single free-text `threshold` string; contract models it as typed `parameters` (record) + ruleType + action — the edit form must build/patch a parameters object, not a string.

items.feature: AML/risk — Create AML rule
items.detail: BE POST /admin/compliance/aml-rules (createAmlRule, step-up) + AmlRuleCreateRequestSchema + client createAmlRule + hook useCreateAmlRule all exist, but the AML design screen offers ONLY per-row edit — no 'Add rule' affordance. A real backend capability with no FE surface; a full rule-management console needs an add-rule form (ruleKey/name/desc/ruleType/action/parameters/enabled). State whether the omission is intentional for launch.

items.feature: AML/risk — Open cases (flagged compliance-event queue) list
items.detail: The 'Open cases' card renders the `OPEN_CASES` const (title/meta/status severity dots). Maps to the real flagged-event queue: GET /admin/compliance/events (listEvents, filterable by status/severity/userId, cursor-paginated) → ComplianceEventListResponseSchema, client listComplianceEvents + hook useComplianceEvents. Wire: replace const with useComplianceEvents({status:'flagged'|'under_review'}). Shape reconciliation: design's title/meta are composed human strings; the DTO gives eventType/severity/ruleOrHit/userId/transactionId/createdAt so the FE must compose the title/meta line. Enum note: design 'escalated' status has no direct contract target (ComplianceEventStatus is flagged/under_review/approved/blocked/dismissed).

items.feature: Compliance — dispose a flagged case/match (approve/block/dismiss/under-review)
items.detail: The design's disposition actions (Sanctions Clear/Escalate/Block; AML case handling) have a real backend: POST /admin/compliance/events/:id/disposition (disposeEvent, step-up-gated, audited as admin_review) with ComplianceDispositionRequestSchema {status: approved|blocked|dismissed|under_review, comment} and client disposeComplianceEvent + hook useDisposeComplianceEvent. Wire the ReasonModal/StepUpModal/MakerCheckerModal chains to this mutation, passing the audited comment. Enum reconciliation: FE 'Clear'→approved/dismissed, 'Block'→blocked, 'Escalate' has no direct target (contract lacks 'escalated' — use under_review or extend the enum). This disposition is on ComplianceEvents, NOT on SanctionsRecords (which are immutable — see the Sanctions rows).

items.feature: Compliance-event detail drill-in (raw screening payload + disposition note)
items.detail: BE GET /admin/compliance/events/:id (getEvent → ComplianceEventDetailSchema with details record, dispositionComment, dispositionAt) + client getComplianceEvent + hook useComplianceEvent exist, but no design screen opens a case-detail view — the AML 'Open cases' rows are not clickable in the mock. Needed for a real case workflow (view the raw provider payload before dispositioning). Small FE-only work to add a detail drawer/modal.

items.feature: AML/risk — Draft SAR/CTR
items.detail: The 'Draft SAR/CTR' link opens a ReasonModal that no-ops. BE POST /admin/compliance/reports (draftReport, step-up, audited) + ComplianceReportDraftRequestSchema {reportType: sar|str, relatedEvents[], content record} + client draftComplianceReport + hook useDraftComplianceReport exist. Wire the modal to build a real draft. Shape gap: design collects only a free-text reason; contract wants reportType + relatedEvents (event ids) + structured content — the modal must pick sar/str and link the case(s). Label note: contract uses 'str' where the design says 'CTR' (SAR/STR vs SAR/CTR to reconcile).

items.feature: Compliance reports — list + submit filed SAR/STR
items.detail: BE GET /admin/compliance/reports (listReports) and POST /admin/compliance/reports/:id/submit (submitReport, step-up, execute) + ComplianceReportListResponseSchema + ComplianceReportSubmitRequestSchema {submissionRef} + clients listComplianceReports/submitComplianceReport + hooks useComplianceReports/useSubmitComplianceReport all exist, but NO design screen shows a reports queue or a submit-with-regulator-ref action. The AML mock only drafts. A real compliance console needs a reports list (draft→submitted→rejected/closed lifecycle) + submit UI.

items.feature: AML/risk — Travel Rule records summary
items.detail: TravelRuleCard hardcodes 'records attached for 3 qualifying transfers over $1,000 in the last 24h'. BE GET /admin/compliance/travel-rule (listTravelRule) → TravelRuleListResponseSchema (items: transactionId, asset, amount, amountFiat, triggeringFactor, capturedAt, reportedAt) + client listTravelRule + hook useTravelRule exist. Wire: replace the static sentence with useTravelRule and count/summarize real items (ideally list them). The $1,000 threshold is itself a config value (compliance.travelRuleThreshold AppSetting), not a constant — read from config, don't hardcode.

items.feature: Sanctions — screening match cards (name · matched list · match-type · numeric confidence score)
items.detail: SanctionsPage renders `SCREENING_MATCHES` consts with a numeric score (0-100), matched-list name (OFAC SDN/EU/UN), and match-type (Name/DOB/Address). The only sanctions endpoint is GET /admin/compliance/sanctions (listSanctions), returning immutable SanctionsRecord history — SanctionsRecordItemSchema has verdict (clear|hit|inconclusive), counterpartyId, provider, screeningType, createdAt — and NO confidence score, NO matched-list name, NO name/DOB/address match-type. So the design's rich match card cannot be populated from the existing DTO. Either read from ComplianceEvents (event `details` JSON may hold the screening payload) or extend the SanctionsRecord schema+repo to surface score/matchedList/matchType. Needs-backend (DTO/schema enrichment) beyond a simple wire.

items.feature: Sanctions — per-match Clear / Escalate / Block disposition
items.detail: Each SanctionsMatchCard offers Clear (Reason) / Escalate (MakerChecker) / Block (Reason→StepUp), flipping to a done-label locally. There is NO disposition endpoint on SanctionsRecords — the sanctions endpoint is read-only immutable history (no updateDisposition on the sanctions repo). Options: (a) re-home these onto POST /admin/compliance/events/:id/disposition (treat a hit as a ComplianceEvent — the intended path, then it's just-wire IF the match is surfaced as an event), or (b) build a dedicated sanctions-disposition endpoint. Because the current screen is driven off SanctionsRecords which have no disposition mutation, classify as needs-backend/decision. 'Block' also semantically implies appending to the blocked list (see Blocked rows).
items.feApiClient: none (disposeComplianceEvent only if re-homed to events)

items.feature: Sanctions — Ongoing monitoring toggles (re-screen daily, screen on outbound, PEP alert, auto-block OFAC)
items.detail: OngoingMonitoring renders `MONITOR_ROWS` consts as controlled Switches that flip locally only. These are policy flags with NO contract and NO endpoint. They belong in the layered config (AppSetting flags like compliance.rescreenDaily / screenOnOutbound / alertNewPep / autoBlockOfac). Needs: register these keys (contracts settings.ts) + persist, then surface via a settings-update client (which also does not exist — see Blocked rows) or a dedicated compliance-policy endpoint. Backend (define+persist flags) + FE settings-client work.

items.feature: Blocked list — read the blocked users/addresses/banks table
items.detail: BlockedPage renders `SEED_ENTRIES` consts (type/value/reason/added-by/when). The store of record is the compliance.sanctionsDenylist AppSetting — a string[] (contracts/admin/settings.ts:184 says 'edited via the existing /admin/settings API, no new endpoint'). Reading it means GET /admin/settings (or /admin/settings/:key) — that BE route exists — BUT web-admin has NO settings api-client and NO settings hook at all (only getPublicConfig reads public/effective config). So the read path needs a new client+hook. ALSO the denylist is a bare string[] with no per-entry reason/added-by/timestamp, so the rich table columns cannot be populated from the current setting shape — either accept a thinner table or model blocked entries as first-class rows (new endpoint/table). Needs-backend: at minimum a settings client; at most a richer blocked-entry model.
items.beContract: EffectiveSettingSchema (value: unknown string[]) — no BlockedEntry DTO

items.feature: Blocked list — Add entry / Remove entry (mutate the sanctions denylist)
items.detail: AddBlockedDialog appends and Remove (Reason→StepUp) deletes, both against local state only. The mutation route EXISTS: PATCH /admin/settings/:key (admin-settings.controller.ts:update, step-up-gated) with UpdateSettingRequestSchema {value, scope, scopeValue} to overwrite compliance.sanctionsDenylist with the new string[]. But there is NO FE settings-update client or hook in web-admin, so both Add and Remove need a `updateSetting` client + hook built and wired (read-modify-write the string[]: append for Add, filter for Remove; there's no per-entry endpoint so the whole recomputed array is sent). Endpoint+contract are ready (just-wire on BE), but the missing FE client makes the FE-visible feature needs-backend-layer work.

items.feature: Audit log — server-side filters (actor / action / date range) + cursor pagination
items.detail: AuditLogQuerySchema supports actorAdminId, subject, action (enum), from/to date range, cursor, limit — all backed by AdminAuditController.list and the useAudit hook. The design exposes only a single free-text search box that filters the 6 mock rows client-side and paginates client-side at size 6. So the DTO's richer filters + keyset pagination are unsurfaced. Wiring the list should also expose action/date filters and switch to nextCursor — otherwise the console can't scan a real (large) audit log. FE-only work atop the existing endpoint.

domains.summary: The Treasury screen and the Reconciliation screen are polar opposites in build state. Treasury has a substantial real backend already built (AdminTreasuryController: balances/exposure/alerts+acknowledge/withdrawal-policies — full controller+service+read-repo+contract+lib client+TanStack hooks), yet treasury-page.tsx renders 100% module-const mock and calls none of it: the four data views it shows partially map to real endpoints (balances→listTreasuryBalances) but the exact cards shown (NGN fiat float, FX position, exposure headroom %) are NOT what the exposure/balances endpoints return, and the two big interactive blocks — the payout/withdrawal approval queue with maker-checker, and the child-address sweeps list — have NO backend at all. Reconciliation is the bigger gap: there is NO admin reconciliation surface anywhere (no controller, contract, lib client, or query hook). Engine-level reconciliation machinery exists (WalletReconciliationService behind POST /admin/wallets/reconcile for per-user on-demand; SettlementReconciliationService webhook-replay worker; a RECONCILIATION_CRON_ENABLED flag) and the engine-brokered remediation primitives exist (POST /admin/transactions/:id/mark-failed and /retry via AdminTxnTriageController), but there is no provider-vs-ledger BREAK read model, no cron-status endpoint, no "run now" trigger endpoint, and no break-resolution/accept/escalate action bound to a break. Net: Treasury = mostly just-wire for balances/exposure/alerts + two mock-only-needs-backend features; Reconciliation = almost entirely mock-only-needs-backend, a full 3-view + 4-action backend must be built (the resolution action can lean on the existing engine triage primitives but needs a break entity to hang off).

items.feature: Treasury: aggregated custodial balances (USDT hero card)
items.detail: FE TREASURY_CARDS[0] 'Custodial · USDT 412,908.44 · 12 wallets · Blockradar TRON' is a hardcoded const. A real endpoint returns SUM(WalletBalance.amount) grouped by network+asset with walletCount — exactly the hero tile's value + '12 wallets · TRON' note. Client + hook already exist. Just swap the const for useTreasuryBalances and map network/asset/totalAmount/walletCount into the hero card. The 'live' flag is already in the FE type.

items.feature: Treasury: exposure headroom / FX position cards
items.detail: FE shows three neutral tiles: 'FX position +$8,240 · Net long USDT vs NGN', 'Exposure headroom 72% · Within inventory limit', and it treats them as simple scalar cards. The real TreasuryExposure DTO returns per-asset rows (cryptoHeld, fiatEquivalent, netExposure, exposureLimitBps, status safe/warning/critical) — it does NOT expose a single 'headroom %' or a signed 'FX position' figure, nor a net-long descriptor. Wiring the headroom card needs a derived headroom = (limit - netExposure)/limit computed either FE-side from the exposure rows or a new summary field; the FX-position card ('+$8,240', 'net long USDT vs NGN') has no backing field and needs a new aggregation (net USDT position valued vs NGN). Classify as needs-backend because the specific numbers the design shows aren't produced by any endpoint.

items.feature: Treasury: NGN fiat-float card + low-float warning banner
items.detail: FE TREASURY_CARDS[1] '₦42,180,500 · 18% of target · low' and the amber LOW_FLOAT banner ('NGN float is at 18% of target') are consts. There is no fiat-float balance endpoint: the treasury balances endpoint aggregates crypto WalletBalance rows only; fiat float lives in the ledger platform_float account (ledger_account_type has 'platform_float'), not surfaced by any treasury read. Needs a new BE aggregation (platform_float balance per fiat currency) plus a configurable target/threshold (an AppSetting) to compute the '% of target' and drive the low-float alert. No contract/client/hook exists.

items.feature: Treasury: exposure-threshold alerts + acknowledge
items.detail: A complete backend feature — list + step-up-guarded, audited acknowledge — with full contract, lib client, AND query hooks (useTreasuryAlerts, useAcknowledgeAlert) already wired. But treasury-page.tsx surfaces NO alerts list or acknowledge action at all; the only banner is the hardcoded LOW_FLOAT one (a different concept). This is ready-built backend awaiting a small FE panel: render the alerts list and wire acknowledge through the existing useStepUpRetry pattern.

items.feature: Treasury: payout / withdrawal approval queue (maker-checker + Approve)
items.detail: The largest Treasury action block: PAYOUTS const (3 rows: 'Kelechi Chukwu · GTBank ₦4,820,000 maker-checker', TRON/Flutterwave payouts) with an Approve button that opens MakerCheckerModal→StepUpModal for big payouts and StepUp for small. There is NO backend: grep for approve-payout/withdrawal-queue/maker-checker across api/src/modules/admin returns nothing. WithdrawalPolicy DTO exists (per-wallet requiresApproval flag) but that is policy config, not a live approval QUEUE of pending withdrawals, and there is no approve endpoint. Building this needs: a pending-withdrawal read model (transactions in a 'awaiting_approval' state or a dedicated ApprovalQueue), a maker-checker dual-control approve endpoint that hands the approved payout to the deterministic engine (never moves money itself, §3.1), contract DTOs, lib client, and hooks. Fully greenfield backend.

items.feature: Treasury: child-address sweeps list + sweep threshold
items.detail: FE SWEEPS const (3 TRON child addresses with TRX balances + Swept/Pending/Below-threshold status) plus a fixed '25 TRX' SWEEP_THRESHOLD footer (comment says it mirrors the sweep.threshold.trx seed setting but has no endpoint). Auto-sweep exists internally in the wallets module (04-wallets.prisma comment: 'deposit webhooks with auto-sweep') but there is NO admin read model exposing per-child-address balances or sweep status, and the threshold is not read from config on this screen. Needs a BE endpoint listing child addresses with on-chain/last-sweep status + the configured threshold (from AppSetting), a contract, client, and hook. The threshold value itself is a config read that could be surfaced via the existing /config layer.

items.feature: Reconciliation: provider-vs-ledger break list (over-credit / missing-settlement / amount-mismatch / duplicate-credit)
items.detail: RECON_BREAKS const (4 breaks with kind, severity, tx ref, detail, signed delta, open/closed status, resolution). There is NO admin reconciliation surface anywhere: no admin-reconciliation.controller, no reconciliation contract in packages/contracts/src/admin, no lib/api/reconciliation.ts, no useRecon* hook. Engine-level reconciliation exists (WalletReconciliationService for per-user on-demand credit; SettlementReconciliationService webhook-replay worker) but neither produces a persisted, queryable BREAK entity with severity/kind/delta. Building this is the core Reconciliation work: a ReconciliationBreak read model (detected provider-vs-ledger discrepancies), a list endpoint with kind/severity/delta/status, contract DTOs, lib client, and query hook. Greenfield.

items.feature: Reconciliation: cron status bar (last/next run, open-breaks count) + 'Run now'
items.detail: FE shows CRON_LAST_RUN '04:00' / CRON_NEXT_RUN '04:00 tomorrow' consts + a client-derived openCount, and the 'Run now' button merely calls router.refresh() — no network call. A RECONCILIATION_CRON_ENABLED config flag exists (default OFF, admin-triggered), and POST /admin/wallets/reconcile runs per-USER on-demand reconciliation, but there is no cron-status read endpoint (last/next run, break count) and no global 'run reconciliation now' trigger endpoint. Needs a status endpoint + a trigger endpoint (or reuse/extend the wallets reconcile job to a platform-wide sweep), contract, client, hook. The per-user reconcile endpoint is close infrastructure but not the same surface.

items.feature: Reconciliation: resolve a break via engine (reason → step-up → double-entry engine action)
items.beEndpoint: none for a break; closest is admin-txn-triage.controller.ts:markFailed/retry (POST /admin/transactions/:id/mark-failed, /retry)
items.beContract: none for a break; closest AdminTxnActionResponse
items.detail: FE 'Resolve via engine' opens ReasonModal→StepUpModal→EngineActionModal with a fabricated double-entry preview (DR user:wallet:usdt / CR recon:adjustment) and idempotencyKey 'recon-{id}-resolve', then flips the break to resolved locally. The engine-brokered remediation PRIMITIVES exist and are exactly the right pattern (AdminTxnTriageService.markFailedAndRefund routes through the engine's atomic refund methods + CompensationRecord, step-up guarded, idempotent, audited; retrySettlement re-enqueues the outbox). But they act on a TRANSACTION id, not a reconciliation break, and there is no 'reverse excess ledger entry' engine action for an over-credit break. Needs a break-resolution endpoint that maps a break to the correct engine action (reverse duplicate credit, post missing settlement, adjust mismatch), reusing the triage service's engine-brokered, idempotent, audited approach. Greenfield endpoint but can lean heavily on existing engine machinery.

items.feature: Reconciliation: accept a break (dual-control, no debit)
items.detail: FE 'Accept' opens MakerCheckerModal with an acceptDiff (Open → 'Accepted (no debit)') and flips the break to accepted locally. No backend: there is no break entity to transition, and no maker-checker accept endpoint. Needs a break-disposition state machine + a dual-control accept endpoint (audited, no money movement), contract, client, hook. Depends on the break read model (feature above) existing first.

items.feature: Reconciliation: escalate a break to a compliance case
items.detail: FE 'Escalate to case' opens ReasonModal then flips the break to 'escalated' locally. Neither side is usably built: no break entity to escalate FROM, and while a compliance module exists (compliance controller/contract/client with events + disposition + reports), there is no 'case' entity that a reconciliation break can be promoted into, and no endpoint linking a recon break to a compliance case. Needs both the break read model AND an escalation endpoint that opens/links a compliance case (or reuses ComplianceEvent creation), with audit. Both-missing because there is no usable target case entity for escalation on the BE and no break entity on either side.

items.feature: Reconciliation: navigate to offending transaction detail
items.detail: Each break card's mono tx button does router.push(`/transactions/${b.tx}`). The transaction-detail route + endpoint + contract + useTransactionDetail hook all already exist (Phase 3 transactions oversight). Once real breaks carry real transaction ids, this link works with zero new backend — the only reason it's not fully 'complete' is the break rows themselves are mock, so the tx ids are fabricated. Trivial once the break list is wired.

domains.domain: Config (settings / pricing / limits / capabilities / assets / currencies / providers / flags)
domains.summary: The Config domain is the strongest "just-wire" opportunity in the admin console: a complete, permissioned, step-up-guarded layered-config backend already exists — `AdminSettingsController` (GET /admin/settings, GET /admin/settings/:key, PATCH /admin/settings/:key), the `EffectiveSetting`/`UpdateSettingRequest` contracts, `AdminSettingsService` (validate → persist → hot-reload → cross-instance invalidate → audited config_change), and a 40+-key `SETTING_REGISTRY` covering pricing spreads/fees/base-rates, NGN tier limits, capability flags, travel-rule, ticketing, and agent. Yet the FE has NO settings api-client (`lib/api/settings.ts` absent) and NO settings hooks (no `useSettings`/`useUpdateSetting` in hooks.ts) — all 8 config screens render module-level mock consts. Read paths for the Asset/Currency catalog DO exist end-to-end (`GET /config` public endpoint + `usePublicConfig` hook) but are unused by the mock screens and expose no contract-address/min-max/live-toggle. The registry drives Settings/Pricing/Limits/Capabilities/Flags edits through ONE generic PATCH — so most edit actions are just-wire. The genuine backend gaps are: currency/asset live-toggle + rounding + name-enquiry, Blockradar catalog sync + discovered-assets, per-tier velocity/weekly/on-chain caps, provider registry + key-reveal(step-up) + test-connection + readiness checklist, and per-cohort/percentage rollout for feature flags. Note: the shared MakerCheckerModal (dual-control) the FE wires every config edit through has NO maker-checker/approvals backend anywhere in the admin module — every "edits enter maker-checker" claim in these screens is currently unbacked; the real PATCH is single-actor with a step-up guard only.

items.feature: Settings — effective-config list (all tunable keys, effective value, DB/ENV/JSON source, description, editable flag)
items.detail: FE settings-page.tsx renders 8 hardcoded SETTING_ROWS. Backend fully exists: GET /admin/settings returns EffectiveSetting[] {key,category,label,description,valueType,editable,value,source('db'|'default'),scope,scopeValue} for every non-secret SETTING_REGISTRY entry. Missing only: create web-admin/lib/api/settings.ts (listEffectiveSettings/getSetting) + useSettings/useSetting hooks + qk.settings key, then render real rows. NOTE the FE's DB>ENV>JSON 3-way 'chain' tooltip is richer than the BE 'source' 2-value enum ('db'|'default') — the ENV-vs-JSON distinction is NOT modeled server-side, so the chain resolution shown is not fully backable without a source enum widening.

items.feature: Settings — edit a DB-layer key (submit new value through step-up)
items.detail: FE Edit pill opens Reason→StepUp→MakerChecker modals but submit is a no-op stub. Backend PATCH /admin/settings/:key exists: AdminStepUpGuard + PermissionGuard('write'), body {value,scope,scopeValue}, validates against per-entry Zod schema (bounds/enum), enforces multi-currency invariant for catalog.* keys, hot-reloads + audits config_change. Missing: updateSetting client fn + useUpdateSetting mutation + wiring the modal's captured value. CAVEAT: the FE promises maker-checker/dual-control ('edits enter Pending approval, then hot-reload'), but the backend applies the change immediately after a single admin's step-up — there is NO maker-checker/approval workflow in the admin module. The step-up guard is the only gate.

items.feature: Pricing — per capability × asset spread / fee / base-rate view + edit
items.detail: FE pricing-page.tsx renders 5 hardcoded PRICING_ROWS. All underlying leaves are registry keys editable via the SAME /admin/settings API: pricing.assets.{USDT,BTC,TRX}.buySpreadBps, .sellSpreadBps, .baseRates.NGN, and pricing.processingFeeBps (category 'Pricing'). So both read and edit are just-wire against GET/PATCH /admin/settings filtered by category=Pricing. Missing: a FE mapper that pivots the flat dot-path settings into per-asset Buy/Sell rows (types/components.ts already anticipates this) and DERIVES the 'user-sees rate' + amber operator margin from baseRate+spread. The min/max column shown per row maps to limits.NGN.*.perTxFiatMax (a different category) — needs cross-category assembly.

items.feature: Limits — per-tier amount caps (per-tx max, daily max, daily tx-count) view + edit
items.detail: FE limits-page.tsx renders hardcoded TIER_SEED. The three core caps per tier ARE registry keys: limits.NGN.{tier_1,tier_2,tier_3}.perTxFiatMax, .dailyFiatMax, .dailyTxCountMax (category 'KYC', positiveInt bounds). Read+edit are just-wire via /admin/settings?category=KYC + PATCH. Missing: a FE mapper that groups the flat keys into the two-card per-tier layout.

items.feature: Limits — extra velocity/count rows shown but NOT in the registry (Weekly max, Single on-chain send max, Sends/10-min window, Cooling-off after tier change, New-beneficiary hold)
items.detail: The FE 'Amount caps' card shows 'Weekly max' + 'Single on-chain send max' and the 'Velocity & counts' card shows 'Transactions/day', 'Sends/10-min window', 'Cooling-off after tier change', 'New-beneficiary hold' per tier. Only 'Transactions/day' maps (limits.NGN.tier.dailyTxCountMax). SETTING_REGISTRY has NO per-tier weekly cap, single-send cap, 10-min send velocity window, or per-tier cooling-off/new-beneficiary-hold. (There IS a single global beneficiary.cryptoCoolingOffSeconds, not per-tier.) These leaves must be added to configuration.ts + SETTING_REGISTRY (and enforced by the engine's velocity/limit checks) before they can be surfaced.

items.feature: Capabilities — crypto.buy/sell/send/receive/swap kill-switch view + toggle
items.detail: FE capabilities-page.tsx renders hardcoded CAPABILITY_SEED. The five crypto capabilities ARE boolean registry keys: catalog.capabilities.crypto.{buy,sell,send,receive,swap} (category 'Catalog'). Toggle = PATCH /admin/settings/:key with a boolean — just-wire via the generic settings API. Missing: settings client/hooks + a FE mapper from the dot-path flags to the switchboard rows (types/components.ts line ~664 already anticipates useSettings('Catalog')). Same maker-checker caveat: FE frames the toggle as dual-control but BE is single-actor + step-up.

items.feature: Capabilities — ticketing vendor rows (ticketing.eventbrite, ticketing.tix) with per-provider port + enable
items.detail: FE shows two ticketing capability rows bound to 'Eventbrite port' / 'Tix.Africa port' with independent enable toggles. The registry only has a single global 'ticketing.enabled' flag (category 'Tickets') and 'ticketing.commissionBps' — there are NO per-vendor capability flags (catalog.capabilities.ticketing.eventbrite / .tix do not exist). Per-vendor enablement + the provider-port binding shown need registry keys + a TicketProvider registry surface built before this is real. The single ticketing.enabled flag IS just-wire but does not match the FE's two-vendor row shape.

items.feature: Assets — asset catalog read (symbol, chain/network, decimals, live/enabled)
items.detail: GET /config (PublicConfigController, unauthenticated) returns enabled assets {symbol,displayName,decimals,networks} + capabilities via AssetRegistry.publicView(), and usePublicConfig() hook already exists in hooks.ts. But assets-page.tsx ignores it and renders hardcoded INITIAL_ASSET_ROWS. Gap for the READ: publicView is filtered to ENABLED-only and strips contract address + min/max (secrets), so it cannot back the FE's 'Contract' column, 'Min/max' column, or the paused/BTC(non-live) rows. Surfacing the full admin asset view (incl. disabled + contract + per-asset min/max) needs an ADMIN assets endpoint, not the public /config. So: the enabled-list read is just-wire against usePublicConfig, but the columns the design shows exceed what /config exposes.

items.feature: Assets — Live toggle (enable/disable a listing), Blockradar catalog sync, 'newly discovered · review to add'
items.detail: FE offers a per-asset Live toggle (maker-checker), a 'Sync Blockradar catalog' action advancing a last-sync line, and a 'Newly discovered' review-to-add card. NONE are backed: there is no catalog.assets.*.enabled registry key for a live toggle (only catalog.capabilities.crypto.* exist; asset enablement lives in the AssetRegistry/JSON catalog, not an admin-editable AppSetting), no admin asset-sync endpoint (grep for sync/discoverAssets in admin/* finds only permission-catalog syncCatalog, unrelated), and no discovered-asset store surfaced to admin. Needs: admin asset-catalog endpoints (list-all incl. disabled, toggle-enabled, trigger Blockradar sync, list-discovered) + repo/service. AssetRegistry already has a discovered-asset overlay internally but it is not exposed to admin.

items.feature: Currencies — fiat catalog read (code, symbol, name, live)
items.detail: GET /config returns enabled fiats {code,displayName,symbol,decimals} and usePublicConfig() exists, but currencies-page.tsx renders hardcoded NGN/RWF/GHS. The enabled-fiat read is just-wire via usePublicConfig; however publicView filters to ENABLED-only, so the FE's off/disabled rows (RWF, GHS) and the 'rounding (dp)'→decimals map partly, but 'name-enquiry availability' is NOT in PublicFiat. So the read is only partially backable; full parity needs an admin fiat view.

items.feature: Currencies — Live toggle (enable/disable a fiat), rounding + name-enquiry configuration
items.detail: FE Live pill toggles a currency through maker-checker; the design also shows editable rounding (dp) + name-enquiry availability. SETTING_REGISTRY has NO catalog.fiats.*.enabled / .rounding / .nameEnquiry keys — fiat enablement lives in the JSON catalog (AssetRegistry), not an admin AppSetting. AdminSettingsService.assertMultiCurrencyInvariant EXISTS and validates catalog.* changes, which implies catalog fiat toggles were intended to be admin-editable, but no such registry key is declared, so PATCH would 404 ('Unknown config key'). Needs catalog.fiats.<code>.enabled (+ rounding/nameEnquiry) registry keys wired to the catalog + the invariant.

items.feature: Providers — WhatsApp Cloud API provider card (non-secret wiring + secret-presence)
items.detail: GET /admin/whatsapp/config exists (WhatsAppConfigView: graphVersion/ids + hasAppSecret/hasFlowPrivateKey/hasVerifyToken booleans, values never returned) and useWhatsAppConfig() hook exists in hooks.ts — but providers-page.tsx hardcodes the WhatsApp card. Surfacing the real WhatsApp provider status/secret-presence is just-wire against the existing hook, but this endpoint only covers WhatsApp, not the other 4 provider cards.

items.feature: Providers — Anthropic/agent provider card (model id, enabled, prompt preview)
items.detail: GET /admin/agent/config exists (AgentConfigView: modelId, enabled, systemPromptPreview; API key never surfaced) with useAgentConfig() hook — the Anthropic card's kind/model line ('claude-opus-4-8') and enablement are backable here. Not surfaced by the mock. Just-wire for that single card; the other provider cards remain unbacked.

items.feature: Providers — Blockradar / Flutterwave / Resend provider cards (status, latency, mock-mode, bound capabilities)
items.detail: FE shows 5 provider cards with live status ('ok'/'degraded'), latency, MOCK-MODE banner, masked API key, and bound-capabilities. Only WhatsApp + Anthropic have read endpoints. There is NO general provider-registry endpoint returning Blockradar/Flutterwave/Resend status+latency+mock-mode+secret-presence+bound-caps. The mock-mode flags DO exist as env (PAYMENTS_MOCK_MODE/WALLET_MOCK_MODE per memory) but are not exposed via an admin provider endpoint. Needs a unified GET /admin/providers (provider registry view with per-provider status/mockMode/secretPresence/boundCapabilities). A live status/latency probe would additionally need a health-check mechanism.

items.feature: Providers — Reveal API key (step-up gated, auto-remask) + Test connection probe
items.detail: FE 'Reveal · step-up' shows a (fake) full secret after a TOTP modal and auto-remasks after 30s; 'Test connection' toasts with no probe. No backend supports either: secret VALUES are deliberately never returned by any admin endpoint (whatsapp/agent DTOs expose only presence booleans, per §3.5), so a reveal-secret endpoint would be a NEW, security-sensitive surface (contradicts current secret-handling posture — likely intentionally omitted; flag for product decision). 'Test connection' needs a per-provider live probe endpoint. Both are net-new backend.

items.feature: Providers — Mock→live readiness checklist
items.detail: FE renders a 5-item readiness checklist (live keys provisioned, mock-mode off, webhook sigs verified, recon cron scheduled, swap route enrolled) with hardcoded done/pending. No backend computes readiness. Needs a GET /admin/providers/readiness (or fold into a provider-registry endpoint) that evaluates env/config posture (mock-mode flags, key presence, cron enablement, swap enrollment). Derivable from config but not exposed today.

items.feature: Flags — product feature flags that ARE registry keys (ticketing.enabled, swap-related, kyc/agent enable)
items.detail: Of the FE FLAG_ROWS, the ones backable by SETTING_REGISTRY are: ticketing.enabled (Tickets), catalog.capabilities.crypto.swap (maps to the FE's 'swap.enabled'), and agent.enabled. These are boolean keys toggled via PATCH /admin/settings — just-wire once the settings client/hooks exist. The FE key names differ from registry dot-paths (e.g. FE 'swap.enabled' vs registry 'catalog.capabilities.crypto.swap'), so a key-mapping layer is needed.

items.feature: Flags — flags with NO registry key (voice_notes.web, voice_notes.whatsapp, beneficiary_flow.whatsapp, kyc.tier_3) + per-cohort/percentage rollout
items.detail: voice_notes.web, voice_notes.whatsapp, beneficiary_flow.whatsapp, and kyc.tier_3 are NOT in SETTING_REGISTRY (voice/media + beneficiary-flow are hard-wired on per memory, not flag-gated). More fundamentally, the FE shows per-cohort / percentage rollout ('gradual · 25% cohort', 'cohort · early access') and an 'eval → on/off' effective-evaluation preview — the layered config is a single global boolean per key with NO cohort/percentage rollout engine at all. Supporting the design needs (a) new boolean registry keys for the unbacked flags AND (b) a genuinely new rollout/targeting subsystem (cohort + percentage evaluation) that does not exist in configuration.ts or EffectiveConfigService.

items.feature: Cross-cutting — Maker-checker / dual-control approval workflow for ALL config edits
items.detail: Every config screen routes edits through the shared MakerCheckerModal and its copy promises 'edits enter Pending approval, then hot-reload' / 'requires a second admin before it takes effect'. There is NO maker-checker/approvals backend in the admin module (no approvals controller/service/table wiring; the separate approvals-page.tsx is itself a mock). The real PATCH /admin/settings/:key applies immediately under a single admin's AdminStepUpGuard — no second-approver, no pending state. Either the FE promise must be dropped to match the single-actor+step-up reality, or a dual-control approval subsystem (proposed-change store, approve/reject, deferred apply) must be built. This affects EVERY config edit action above.

domains.summary: Comms has a sharp split. The TEMPLATES sub-domain is fully built on the backend (Prisma-backed CRUD + deterministic preview at /admin/notification-templates, contracts, lib/api clients, and a fully-wired TemplateEditorDialog + hooks) — but the design-repro TemplatesPage renders 6 mock cards and never imports the editor or calls useNotificationTemplates, so every templates feature is a pure "just-wire". WhatsApp has ONE real endpoint (GET /admin/whatsapp/config, non-secret wiring + secret-presence flags) that WhatsAppPage ignores, plus the config view omits every operational metric the design health card shows (quality rating, messaging limit, webhook health, template rejections) — those need backend. NOTIFICATIONS is emptiest: broadcast composer, delivery log, bounce/complaint rates, WhatsApp Flows registry, live conversation monitor, and the topbar alerts feed have NO endpoint/contract/service — all mock-only-needs-backend. Net: ~5 just-wire, ~9 mock-only-needs-backend, 1 backend-only-not-surfaced (composite-key GET-one + PATCH edit exists in the dialog but no page opens it). Phasing: Phase 1 wire templates list+editor (backend done) and whatsapp config; Phase 2 build WhatsApp health/metrics + Flows registry + conversation monitor; Phase 3 build the broadcast engine + delivery log + bounce/complaint + alerts feed (all net-new, maker-checker-gated).

items.feature: Templates list (grid of template cards: channel chip, key, locale, vars, body)
items.detail: TemplatesPage (templates-page.tsx) renders module-level const TEMPLATE_ROWS of 6 fabricated cards. Real GET /admin/notification-templates (Prisma-backed via NOTIFICATION_TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY), NotificationTemplateListResponse contract, listNotificationTemplates() client, and useNotificationTemplates() hook (30s stale) ALL exist and go unused. Wiring = replace the const with the hook + loading/error/empty/data branches. NOTE the design's `approval` pill (Approved/Pending/Rejected) is NOT a field on the real NotificationTemplate DTO (it has no approval/status) — that one sub-field is mock-only-needs-backend if an approval workflow is wanted.

items.feature: Template create (New template editor: key/language/channel/subject/contentText/contentHtml/whatsappTemplateId/variables + step-up)
items.detail: A complete TemplateEditorDialog (template-editor-dialog.tsx) is already wired to useUpsertTemplate -> upsertNotificationTemplate() -> POST /admin/notification-templates (step-up-guarded, audited as config_change) with NotificationTemplateUpsertRequestSchema parse + useStepUpRetry. It is NOT imported or mounted by TemplatesPage (grep confirms no reference in app/ or the page). Wiring = add an 'Add template' trigger + <TemplateEditorDialog template={null}> on the page. Backend + client + hook + dialog all done; only the page mount is missing.

items.feature: Template edit (open a card -> edit existing, immutable composite key, PATCH)
items.detail: PATCH /admin/notification-templates/:templateKey/:language/:channel (step-up, audited) + updateNotificationTemplate() client + the isEdit branch of TemplateEditorDialog (immutable key/lang/channel) all exist. But TemplatesPage renders static cards with NO click handler / no editor trigger (the page's own comment states the design markup is read-only). Needs FE work: make each card open <TemplateEditorDialog template={row}>. The GET-one (get()) endpoint + getNotificationTemplate() + useNotificationTemplate() also exist but are unused since the list already carries full rows.

items.feature: Template live preview (deterministic render of content + sample variables JSON)
items.detail: PreviewPanel inside TemplateEditorDialog is fully wired to usePreviewTemplate -> previewNotificationTemplate() -> POST /admin/notification-templates/preview (pure renderTemplate, no persistence). This becomes end-to-end the moment the dialog is mounted (see the create/edit rows). Listed separately because it is the one Comms feature genuinely wired FE->BE inside its (currently unmounted) component.

items.feature: WhatsApp wiring view (phone number ID, WABA/app ids, graph version, Flow ids, secret-presence flags)
items.detail: WhatsAppPage HealthCard renders a WA_HEALTH const with masked number/id. GET /admin/whatsapp/config (AdminWhatsAppConfigService, reads layered env, returns non-secret ids + hasAppSecret/hasFlowPrivateKey/hasVerifyToken), WhatsAppConfigView contract, getWhatsAppConfig() client, useWhatsAppConfig() hook ALL exist and are unused. Wiring = replace WA_HEALTH with the hook, rendering graphVersion/phoneNumberId/wabaId/appId/flowId/beneficiaryFlowId + presence booleans. Design's masked display number is NOT in the DTO (only phoneNumberId) — minor: show phoneNumberId or add displayNumber to the config view.

items.feature: WhatsApp operational health metrics (quality rating GREEN/High, messaging limit tier, webhook subscribed/200, last-webhook age, template rejections 7d)
items.detail: WA_HEALTH shows live Cloud-API operational signals (quality rating, per-tier messaging limit, webhook subscription status, last-webhook timestamp, 7d template-rejection count). NONE are in WhatsAppConfigView (pure static wiring + secret-presence). No endpoint/contract/service fetches them from the Meta Graph API or from stored webhook receipts. Needs backend: a WhatsApp health service querying Graph (phone_number quality/limit) + deriving webhook liveness from stored inbound events + counting template rejections, plus a new contract, client, hook.

items.feature: WhatsApp 'ban-risk: low / Official Cloud API only' assurance note
items.detail: HealthCard renders a static success note. If meant to be a real computed posture (e.g. derived from quality rating + no-unofficial-automation), it needs backing; today it is a hardcoded string with no endpoint. Could ride the health-metrics endpoint above as a derived field, or be accepted as a static assurance label (intentional-static — needs a product decision).

items.feature: WhatsApp Flows registry (KYC / itemized confirmation / PIN entry rows with Live pills)
items.detail: FlowsCard renders WA_FLOWS const (3 hardcoded flows, all live:true). WhatsAppConfigView exposes flowId + beneficiaryFlowId only — not a per-flow registry with name/description/published-status. No endpoint lists registered Flows or their live state from Meta. Needs backend: a Flows list (id, name, desc, published/live) built from config-registered flow ids checked against the Graph Flows API, plus contract/client/hook. The two flow ids in config are a partial seed; per-flow name/desc/live status is net-new.

items.feature: WhatsApp live conversation monitor (read-only redacted inbound/outbound chat bubbles)
items.detail: ConversationMonitorCard renders WA_CONVO const (4 fabricated redacted bubbles). There is NO WhatsApp-conversation endpoint. The closest existing surface is GET /admin/agent/conversations (admin-agent.controller.ts, listConversations()/getConversation(), ConversationLogList contract) — but that is the AGENT domain's channel-agnostic intent log, not a WhatsApp-specific redacted live-message monitor. Needs backend: a WhatsApp inbound/outbound message read model with PII redaction, list/detail contract, client, hook, and a live/polling story. Reusing the agent log would need a channel=whatsapp filter + message-level redaction that don't exist today. Largest Comms build.

items.feature: Broadcast composer audience cohorts with reach counts (Lagos / tier_1 / verified / all)
items.detail: BroadcastComposer AUDIENCE_OPTIONS + AUDIENCE_REACH are hardcoded consts (fabricated cohort labels + reach numbers). No endpoint returns segmentable audiences or their live sizes. Needs backend: an audiences/cohorts service (query the user base by cohort predicate, return count), contract, client, hook. The LARGE_AUDIENCE_THRESHOLD (10000) that flips maker-checker is also a hardcoded FE literal that should be a config-sourced (AppSetting) value per root §7.

items.feature: Broadcast send / queue-for-approval (maker-checker on large audience, template + schedule)
items.detail: The composer's send only opens a MakerCheckerModal then calls pushToast + setQueued(true) — nothing is submitted. No POST /admin/broadcasts, no broadcast contract, no service, no maker-checker approval persistence. Needs backend: a broadcast create endpoint (audience + templateKey + schedule now/tomorrow-9/custom), a proposal-only + maker-checker approval flow for large audiences (mirroring engine-disposes), idempotency, and integration with the notifications delivery pipeline. The composer's TEMPLATE dropdown (kyc_reminder/tx_confirmation/promo_ticketing) is a separate hardcoded const that should draw from the real template list. Largest net-new action.

items.feature: Broadcast schedule options (Send now / Tomorrow 9:00 / Custom datetime)
items.detail: SCHEDULE_OPTIONS const + a datetime-local input feed a broadcast POST body that does not exist. Part of the broadcast-send backend above, but the scheduling semantics (queue-at-time) are a distinct concern (a scheduler/cron consuming scheduled broadcasts). No endpoint/contract today.

items.feature: Delivery log (per-message channel chip + template name + audience + time + status Delivered/Sent/Sending/Bounced/Queued/Scheduled/Failed)
items.detail: DeliveryLog renders DELIVERY_ROWS const (5 fabricated rows). No endpoint returns sent-message delivery records with per-channel status. Needs backend: a notification/delivery read model (message log with channel, template, audience, sent-at, provider delivery status), contract, client, hook, likely paginated. The schema models message delivery elsewhere (ReceiptDeliveryStatus in transactions) but there is no admin-facing notifications delivery-log read path.

items.feature: Bounce / complaint rate footnote (bounce 0.4% · complaint 0.02% via Resend)
items.detail: Hardcoded string in the DeliveryLog header. No endpoint aggregates Resend (email) bounce/complaint webhooks into rates. Needs backend: ingest Resend bounce/complaint webhooks (or query Resend), aggregate into rates over a window, expose on a metrics/delivery-log endpoint, contract, client, hook.

items.feature: Topbar operator alerts feed (reconciliation break / sanctions hit / stuck-settlement + unread badge)
items.detail: NotificationsMenu (notifications-menu.tsx, the bell dropdown) renders an ALERTS const of 3 hardcoded operator alerts with unread=ALERTS.length; its own comment says 'there is no alerts-feed endpoint yet'. No endpoint/contract aggregates cross-domain operational alerts (recon breaks, sanctions hits, stuck txns) into an admin alert feed. Needs backend: an operator-alerts aggregation endpoint (or per-domain alert counts), contract, client, hook, plus unread/ack semantics. Cross-cutting but surfaced in the notifications chrome.

domains.summary: The two design screens (tickets-page.tsx, agent-page.tsx) are pure design reproductions rendering module-level mock consts with zero fetching. The backend built earlier covers only a thin read-only slice: Tickets exposes ONLY a ticket-order list (GET /admin/tickets/orders) — its "Recent orders" panel is a clean just-wire.
