Agent exposes a config view (modelId/enabled/prompt-preview) plus conversation-log list+detail with full clients, hooks, and even an already-wired-but-unmounted conversation-log-detail.tsx component — but the design's Agent screen surfaces NONE of that (it shows guardrails/prompt-versions/tool-registry/usage instead, all of which lack any backend). Net: of ~12 concrete features, exactly ONE (ticket orders) is a clean just-wire; the Vendor-ports panel and the entire Agent screen's four panels are mock-only-needs-backend or settings-adjacent; conversation logs are a substantial backend-only-not-surfaced capability the design forgot. The vendor enablement/commission and agent model/enablement values exist as /admin/settings registry keys (ticketing.enabled, ticketing.commissionBps, agent.enabled, agent.modelId) but there is NO settings client/hook in web-admin and no vendor-ports LIST endpoint, so those pills cannot be wired without either the settings CRUD client or a new vendor-registry endpoint. Guardrail params (checkpointer, max tool calls), prompt-version maker-checker workflow, tool-registry listing, and 24h cost/usage/token telemetry have no backend at all.

items.feature: Tickets: Recent orders list (event/id · user · amount · payment+settlement status)
items.detail: The design's RecentOrdersCard renders ORDER_ROWS mock consts. A complete backend read path already exists: GET /admin/tickets/orders (AdminTicketsController.listOrders) → AdminTicketService.listOrders → ITicketOrderReadRepository keyset pagination, contract TicketOrderItem/TicketOrderListResponse, client listTicketOrders(), hook useTicketOrders(), qk.ticketOrders. Just replace ORDER_ROWS with useTicketOrders() and add loading/error/empty branches. NOTE shape drift the FE must map: BE returns paymentStatus + settlementStatus + deliveryStatus + ticketType + quantity + userId (uuid), whereas the mock collapses to a single `status` + a human `user` name + a preformatted `amt` string and an `event` label. There is no user-name join and no event/title field on TicketOrderItem — FE must render vendorKey/ticketType and userId (or add a join server-side), and format totalAmount (canonical NGN string) itself. Cursor pagination (nextCursor) is available but the mock has no 'load more'.

items.feature: Tickets: Vendor ports list (port name · commission · live/paused/onboarding status)
items.detail: The design's VendorPortsCard renders VENDOR_ROWS mock consts (ticketing.eventbrite 6.5% live, ticketing.tix 5.0% onboarding). There is NO endpoint, contract, service, or repository that lists registered ticketing vendor ports. The only related backend is generic /admin/settings registry keys ticketing.enabled (single platform flag) and ticketing.commissionBps (single platform commission) — a SINGLE vertical-wide flag+commission, NOT a per-vendor list with per-vendor status/commission as the design implies. Per CLAUDE.md §7 each ticketing.<vendor> should be a registered provider port behind an admin flag, but no such registry is enumerated over an endpoint. Building this requires: a vendor-port registry read endpoint (GET /admin/tickets/vendors), a contract DTO (name/commissionBps/status), and a service that reads the registered TicketProvider ports + their layered enablement flags. Also note the design's three-state status (live/paused/onboarding) is richer than the boolean enablement flag that exists.
items.beContract: none (only settings.ts registry keys ticketing.enabled + ticketing.commissionBps)

items.feature: Tickets: Event catalog (headed 'Vendor ports, event catalog, orders and vendor payout reconciliation')
items.detail: The page subheader promises an event catalog but neither the design nor the backend implements it — there is no catalog panel in tickets-page.tsx and no events endpoint/contract/service anywhere in admin. There is no tickets domain module at all (AdminTicketService comment: 'There is NO tickets module'); only existing TicketOrder rows are projected. Building event-catalog oversight needs the whole tickets vertical (event ingestion from vendor ports, an Event entity/repo, and an admin list endpoint) — out of scope for a repro-screen wire-up and effectively a new vertical.

items.feature: Tickets: Vendor payout reconciliation (also promised in subheader)
items.detail: Subheader promises 'vendor payout reconciliation' but there is no panel in the design and no reconciliation endpoint/contract/service. settlementStatus exists on TicketOrderItem (pending/settled/refunded/failed) but there is no payout-batch or vendor-reconciliation aggregation surface. Would require a new reconciliation read model (per-vendor owed/paid/pending rollups) plus endpoint+contract — a full feature, not a wire-up.

items.feature: Agent: Model & guardrails panel — Model id + Enabled
items.detail: AGENT_PARAMS mock hardcodes Model=claude-opus-4-8. Two of these fields are real: GET /admin/agent/config (AdminAgentController.getConfig → AdminAgentService.getConfig) returns modelId + enabled (both from EffectiveConfigService) + systemPromptPreview, via contract AgentConfigView, client getAgentConfig(), hook useAgentConfig(). So 'Model' and an enablement indicator can be wired directly from useAgentConfig(). The mock does NOT currently show systemPromptPreview even though the backend returns it — a small addition. Only the model-id/enabled rows are just-wire; the other three rows in this panel are separate (see next).

items.feature: Agent: Guardrail params — Structured output / Checkpointer / PIN+step-up / Max tool calls per turn
items.detail: Four of the five AGENT_PARAMS rows (Structured output='IntentSchema (enforced)', Checkpointer='none (extractable)', PIN+step-up='required to execute', Max tool calls/turn='6') are static mock strings with NO backend. AgentConfigView returns only modelId/enabled/systemPromptPreview. These are architectural facts (some genuinely static/constant per §3.1/§6) — but if they are to be operator-visible/config-driven they need either (a) additional read-only fields on AgentConfigView sourced from the agent runtime/layered config (e.g. agent.maxToolCallsPerTurn), or (b) an accepted decision to keep them as FE-side static constants documenting the architecture. 'Max tool calls / turn = 6' in particular smells like it should be a config value (§7) but no such registry key exists. Recommend: extend AgentConfigView with a small set of read-only guardrail booleans/numbers rather than leaving four hardcoded strings.

items.feature: Agent: System-prompt versions panel (v4.2.0 live / v4.3.0 staged / v4.1.3 archived, View diff/Review/Restore, maker-checker)
items.detail: PROMPT_VERSIONS mock renders a full versioned prompt-management workflow with maker-checker (promoted-by, awaiting-checker, rolled-back) and action buttons (View diff/Review/Restore) that currently only pushToast. There is NO backend for this and it directly CONTRADICTS the current invariant: AdminAgentService/AgentConfigView expose only a read-only systemPromptPreview string and the code+contract comments explicitly state the system prompt is 'read-only and never editable (§3.1/§6)' and 'NOT registered' in settings. So a versioned, promotable, restorable prompt store with a maker-checker approval flow is a substantial new capability (schema for prompt versions + status, promote/review/restore endpoints with maker-checker + audit, diff endpoint) that also requires a product/architecture decision to reverse the 'prompt is not editable' stance. Flag for triage before building.

items.feature: Agent: Tool registry list (get_quote/get_wallet_balance/... read + propose_buy/sell/send/swap write chips)
items.detail: TOOL_ROWS mock hardcodes 8 tool names with read/write kind chips. There is NO endpoint/contract/service that enumerates the agent's registered tool registry with each tool's kind. The real tools live in the agent module's typed tool layer (modules/agent), but nothing projects them to the admin surface. Building this needs a read-only tool-registry endpoint (GET /admin/agent/tools) + contract (name + kind: read|write) whose source is the agent's ToolGateway/tool definitions. Must respect §3.2 (admin cannot import agent internals directly) — likely a small registry-descriptor the agent module exposes. Static-ish data but currently zero backend.

items.feature: Agent: Cost & usage (24h) — Conversations / Input tokens / Output tokens / Est. cost
items.detail: AGENT_USAGE mock hardcodes 1,842 conversations / 1,284,930 input tokens / 312,547 output tokens / $48.20 est cost. There is NO usage/cost/token telemetry endpoint anywhere in admin (grep for token/usage/cost in admin returns only auth-token and metrics-window code, no LLM usage aggregation). Requires capturing per-call token usage from the LLM provider adapter, persisting it, and an aggregation read endpoint (GET /admin/agent/usage?range=24h) + contract with token counts and a cost computation (needs per-model pricing config). Substantial: new persistence + aggregation + pricing config. Note admin-metrics module exists for other operational metrics but does not cover agent token/cost.

items.feature: Agent: Conversation / intent logs — list + detail (messages, per-message intent, replies)
items.detail: A complete backend + FE client layer exists and is UNUSED by the design's Agent screen. Backend: GET /admin/agent/conversations (list) and GET /admin/agent/conversations/:id (detail with messages+per-message intent action/confidence+replies) via AdminAgentController + AdminAgentService (ConversationLogItem/ConversationLogDetail contracts), clients listConversations()/getConversation(), hooks useConversations()/useConversation(), qk.conversations/conversation. There is even an already-built component web-admin/components/admin/conversation-log-detail.tsx that consumes useConversation — but it is NOT mounted in any route and agent-page.tsx does not reference it. This is a real oversight capability (agent intent auditing, directly supporting §3.1 'model proposes' visibility) that the design screen simply omits. Needs FE work: add a conversations list + detail section (or a dedicated sub-screen) to the Agent surface and mount the existing conversation-log-detail component. Low backend risk (fully built), medium FE effort (new list view + wiring). Not an intentional omission — the built-but-unmounted component indicates it was intended.

items.feature: Agent: System-prompt preview (read-only) surfaced to operators
items.detail: AgentConfigView.systemPromptPreview is a real backend field (a fixed read-only description of the agent's role, deliberately not the live prompt, never editable) returned by GET /admin/agent/config and parsed by client getAgentConfig(). The design's Agent screen never displays it — the prompt is instead (mis)represented by the mock 'System-prompt versions' panel. Wiring is trivial (render config.systemPromptPreview in a read-only card). Distinct from the versions/maker-checker feature above, which the backend intentionally does NOT support.

items.feature: Tickets/Agent: editing vendor commission/enablement & agent model/enablement (settings-adjacent)
items.detail: The design shows vendor commission and 'read-mostly' agent params as display-only, but the actual tunable values live in the generic settings registry: ticketing.enabled, ticketing.commissionBps, agent.enabled, agent.modelId (packages/contracts/src/admin/settings.ts), writable via GET/GET:key/PATCH /admin/settings (AdminSettingsController). However there is NO settings client or hook in web-admin (grep found no listSettings/updateSetting/useSettings; admin.ts has no settings fn) and settings-page.tsx is itself a pure mock whose keys (agent.model, ticketing.commission.pct) do not even match the real registry keys (agent.modelId, ticketing.commissionBps). So to make the tickets/agent screens' enablement/commission/model actionable (or even to correctly reflect effective values beyond agent config), a settings CRUD client+hook must be built and pointed at the real keys. Backend fully exists; FE plumbing (client + hook + correct keys) is missing across the whole settings surface, which these two domains depend on for their write-side values.

domains.domain: Metrics & Dashboard (operator admin console — home "/" mock OperatorDashboard vs. wired "/metrics" MetricsDashboard + admin-metrics backend)
domains.summary: The target FE mock is web-admin/components/admin/operator-dashboard.tsx (rendered at home "/" via app/page.tsx), which renders entirely module-level mock consts. A SEPARATE, fully-wired real dashboard already exists at web-admin/components/admin/metrics-dashboard.tsx (rendered at "/metrics"), backed by GET /admin/metrics/{dashboard,transactions,revenue,kyc-funnel} (admin-metrics.controller.ts) with contracts in admin-metrics.dto.ts and client metrics.ts / hook useDashboardMetrics. So the metrics-family data views are "just-wire" against the existing composite endpoint (the home screen simply renders mock instead of calling getDashboardMetrics). The gaps are the NON-metrics widgets the mock invented: GMV KPI (no backend), a per-day-per-capability STACKED volume series (backend only gives a flat daily total + per-type totals, not a cross-tab), System health with provider LATENCY + webhook-queue depth + recon-drift (no backend at all), a Live activity feed (no backend), an "Approvals awaiting me" maker-checker inbox (NO approvals/maker-checker controller, contract, or lib client anywhere), and the Alerts card (sanctions + treasury alerts + compliance events have real endpoints but no unified "dashboard alerts" feed, and "provider incident" has no source). Recommended build order: Phase 1 wire the metrics-family KPIs/charts on the home screen to the existing composite (or just route "/" to the real MetricsDashboard); Phase 2 build the maker-checker approvals inbox + activity feed (both entirely missing); Phase 3 build system-health/provider-latency + a unified alerts aggregator and GMV/stacked-series aggregations.

To show a money figure you either surface counts (just-wire) or add a summed-amount aggregation (then it becomes mock-only-needs-backend). Counts are wire-ready; a fiat-notional volume sum is not.

items.detail: Mock KPI_DEFS[1] shows GMV base 41,209,800. grep for gmv/grossMerchandise across contracts + api returns nothing. No ledger/transaction aggregation sums gross notional. Needs a new repo aggregation (sum of transaction fiat notionals over range) + a field on RevenueMetrics/DashboardSummary + FE wiring.

items.feature: Revenue (fees + FX) KPI tile

So 'fees' wire directly; the '+ FX' (spread) portion of the label cannot be honored without new ledgering — surface fees only, drop the FX claim, or spawn spread-ledgering work.

items.detail: Mock KPI_DEFS[3] base 1284. Real dashboard already derives totalTxns = sum(byType.count) in metrics-dashboard.tsx KpiGrid. Pure wire — sum byType counts client-side.

items.feature: Failed / stuck tx KPI tile (attention/warn)

'Stuck' (pending_settlement) is a distinct status not in the failed bucket — the byType.count minus completed minus failed captures pending, so a true failed+stuck figure needs a small client derivation (or a pending field). Mostly wire; pending-status count needs surfacing.

items.feature: Open compliance cases KPI tile (attention/warn)

items.feature: Transaction volume chart — daily bars stacked by capability (buy/sell/send/swap/ticket)

items.feature: System health — provider list with latency (Blockradar/Flutterwave/Resend/WhatsApp/Anthropic + ms)
items.detail: Mock HEALTH const shows 5 named providers with dot color + latency ('120ms', '890ms'). No backend measures provider latency/health. A real provider-health probe (ping/circuit-breaker/last-webhook-age per external client) + endpoint + contract must be built. Largest single gap here.

items.detail: Mock MY_APPROVALS (3 items) + the /approvals route + MakerCheckerModal render a from→to diff and 'submit for second approval' flow. items.feature: Approvals — 'Open inbox →' link + open a pending approval (maker-checker modal submit)
items.detail: The mock's onSubmit just navigates to /approvals with no API call; the /approvals page itself is also a design repro with no wired client. No approval-disposition endpoint exists. items.feature: Alerts — Sanctions hit (name match) row → /sanctions
items.detail: Mock ALERTS[0] is a static sanctions-match card linking to /sanctions. Real sanctions screening-run history (useSanctions) and flagged compliance events (useComplianceEvents) endpoints exist. items.feature: Alerts — Over-credit flagged row → /reconciliation
items.detail: Mock ALERTS[1] 'tx_80257 +70.00 USDT above ledger. Not auto-debited.' No endpoint surfaces over-credit/ledger-drift flags. items.detail: Mock ALERTS[2] 'Flutterwave NGN payouts degraded' links to /ops. No provider-incident/status source exists (ties to the missing System-health provider probe). Needs the provider-health backend before this alert can be real.

items.detail: The backend computes activeUsers (activeInRange/newInRange/totalUsers) and the real MetricsDashboard surfaces it, but the MOCK OperatorDashboard has NO active-users tile (it shows New signups only). domains.summary: The RBAC & Admins domain is split: /roles and /sessions are already fully real-wired FE→BE (complete), but the two screens the task names — /admins (AdminsPage) and /admin-settings (AdminSettingsPage) — are still design mocks rendering module-level consts, even though a complete backend (admin-users/roles/sessions/auth/invitation controllers + services + repos), contracts, api-client (lib/api/admin.ts), and query hooks all exist. Crucially, real-wired FE building blocks already exist but sit UNMOUNTED: AdminRowActions (role/status change with step-up), RolePermissionMatrix (real derived matrix), and the useAdmins hook — the routed /admins page just doesn't import them. items.detail: Step-up is fully wired for the real admin row actions: AdminStepUpService challenge, AdminStepUpGuard on PATCH role/status, and FE useStepUpRetry + StepUpDialog that catch ADMIN_STEP_UP_REQUIRED 403 and retry after re-auth (password vs TOTP chosen off useAdminMe().mfaEnabled). Complete on the real path. NOTE the MOCK AdminsPage instead uses cosmetic StepUpModal/ReasonModal/MakerCheckerModal stubs from components/admin/flows with no side effects — those get discarded when /admins is wired to AdminRowActions.

items.detail: RequirePermission is a real, working UX gate that reads useAdminMe().pages/menus/role and hides page bodies for un-granted operators (API still enforces via PermissionGuard/default-deny). It exists and works, but confirm each RBAC route (app/admins, app/roles, app/sessions, app/admin-settings pages) actually wraps its content in RequirePermission with the correct web_page resourceId. If any of the four is unwrapped, wiring = wrap it. Low effort; purely FE composition. Server-side enforcement is already complete.

domains.summary: Both screens are pure design reproductions rendering module-level mock consts — NO api client, NO query hook, NO route-level fetch on either. The Approvals maker-checker inbox has ZERO backend: no ChangeRequest/ApprovalRequest Prisma model, no controller, no contract DTO, no dual-control anywhere (admin settings PATCH / KYC approve / tier override all apply DIRECTLY with a single admin, no second-approver queue). So the entire approval-request lifecycle (raise → awaiting-me/mine buckets → approve → reject-with-reason) is mock-only and must be BUILT — though the underlying mutations each kind wraps (settings PATCH, txn retry/mark-failed, KYC approve, tier set) mostly already exist. The Ops screen likewise has no ops/jobs API: serviceHealth exists but is buy/sell/send/swap SUCCESS-RATE metrics, NOT provider latency/uptime tiles; there is no webhook-queue-depth endpoint and no generic cron-job list/run-now endpoint. The only real ops primitives are Bull Board (Basic-auth Express dashboard, not a JSON API), the BackfillRun enqueue/poll + wallet reconcile endpoints (two specific jobs, permission-gated, engine-brokered), and the BullMQ JobQueue port. Recommended phasing: P1 build the maker-checker ChangeRequest engine + approvals inbox endpoints (highest value, funds-safety-adjacent, entirely missing); P2 build the ops read endpoints (provider health probe, webhook-queue depth, cron-job registry) surfacing existing BullMQ/BackfillRun/reconcile as first-class "run now" jobs; P3 wire the FE screens to both.

items.feature: Approvals inbox — list dual-control change-requests (Awaiting me / My requests buckets with count badges)
items.detail: FE ApprovalsPage renders SAMPLE_REQUESTS (4 hardcoded consts, id/kind/title/by/byRole/ago/resource/reason/diff) and computes awaiting/mine by comparing byRole to a hardcoded ROLE='super_admin'. There is NO backend for a maker-checker approval queue anywhere: no ApprovalRequest/ChangeRequest Prisma model (schema has only AuditLog + BackfillRun as run-like models; 03-admin.prisma has AdminUser/AdminSession/Role/Permission/RolePermissionAssignment/AdminInvitation — no change-request), no controller route, no contract DTO, no lib/api client, no query hook. Building this requires a whole dual-control engine: a ChangeRequest model (kind, target resource, proposed diff, maker adminId+role, status, reason), a GET /admin/approvals?bucket= endpoint that partitions by whether the current admin is the maker, and permission gating (only approver roles see actions). This is the core missing piece.

items.feature: Approve a change-request (applies the pending change after a second admin confirms)
items.detail: FE Approve button (RequestCard, gated by CAN_APPROVE=true && !mine) just calls dismiss(request.id) to remove the local row — no network, no modal. No POST /admin/approvals/:id/approve endpoint, DTO, client, or hook exists. Building it means: a ChangeRequest lifecycle service that, on second-admin approval, atomically applies the deferred mutation (e.g. settings PATCH, capability flip, tier set, refund) via the SAME underlying service the maker would have called, records the approver in the immutable AuditLog, and enforces maker≠approver (the FE's 'your own request needs a different admin' guard must be server-side, root §3.3). Funds-relevant kinds (Refund) must route through the engine, never a raw side-effect. The underlying per-kind mutations largely exist (settings.service PATCH, txn-triage retry/mark-failed, kyc-review approve, end-user tier) — what's missing is the deferred-apply-on-approval orchestration.

items.feature: Reject a change-request with a reason (ReasonModal flow)
items.detail: FE Reject opens the shared ReasonModal (design rejectItem → runFlow(['reason'])) and on continue just dismisses the local row (confirmReject → dismiss). No POST /admin/approvals/:id/reject endpoint, DTO, client, or hook. Building it: a reject transition on the ChangeRequest service that captures the mandatory reason, marks the request rejected without applying the change, and audits the rejector. Depends on the ChangeRequest model/engine from the inbox item above; smaller than approve because it applies nothing.

items.feature: Maker-checker enforcement of high-risk config changes (pricing spread, capability flip, tier override) — the write path that CREATES an approval request
items.detail: The approvals inbox implies that certain admin mutations must ENQUEUE a change-request instead of applying immediately. Today they apply directly with one admin: admin-settings.controller PATCH /admin/settings/:key (used for the 'Pricing change' and 'Capability' approval kinds) writes straight through admin-settings.service (grep for dual/maker/checker/pendingChange in that service = zero matches); admin-end-users tier set and admin-kyc-review approve are also single-admin. So the 'requires a second admin before it takes effect' promise in the page header is entirely unimplemented server-side. Building it: a policy that classifies which settings keys / capabilities / tier jumps are high-risk and, for those, diverts the write into a ChangeRequest (status=pending) rather than committing — the maker path of the maker-checker loop.

items.feature: Refund approval kind (partial refund of a transaction, engine-brokered)
items.detail: The 'Refund' approval row (apr_5003, ₦180,000 partial refund of tx_80257) references a refund capability that does not exist as either an approval OR a direct action. admin-transactions.controller exposes only GET /transactions and GET /transactions/:id (read-only); admin-txn-triage.controller has POST /transactions/:id/mark-failed and /retry but NO refund route. There is no refund DTO, service, client, or hook. So a refund needs BOTH an engine-brokered refund execution path (build in transactions/engine, funds-moving → §3.1: propose→validate→idempotency-key→execute) AND its maker-checker wrapper. Highest-risk item; do not ship without the deterministic engine path.

items.feature: Provider status board — per-provider health tiles (Blockradar/Flutterwave/Resend/WhatsApp/Anthropic) with latency + Operational/Degraded status
items.detail: FE OpsPage renders PROVIDER_TILES (5 hardcoded consts with fake latencies/status). No backend provider-health probe exists. The nearest thing — AdminMetricsService.dashboard's serviceHealth (contracts ServiceHealthMetricsSchema, GET /admin/metrics/dashboard) — is NOT this: it reports per-transactable-SERVICE (buy/sell/send/swap) total/completed/failed/successRate computed from Transaction rows, not per-external-PROVIDER latency/uptime. Building the tiles needs a new health/probe endpoint that pings each registered provider adapter (or reads a health cache) and returns {name, latencyMs, status}. Entirely new contract + service + client + hook.

items.feature: Webhook queues panel — per-ingest-queue depth + retries + health (blockradar.deposit/withdraw, flutterwave.collection, whatsapp.inbound)
items.detail: FE renders WEBHOOK_QUEUES (4 hardcoded consts: name/depth/retries/status). No JSON endpoint exposes queue depth/retries. A BullMQ JobQueue port exists (core/jobs/application/job-queue.port.ts) and Bull Board is mounted at /admin/queues, but Bull Board is an HTML dashboard behind Basic-auth Express middleware (bull-board.middleware.ts) — not a typed JSON API the FE can consume, and it's queue metrics for BullMQ jobs, not inbound-webhook ingest queues specifically. Building this needs a GET /admin/ops/queues endpoint that reads BullMQ queue counts (waiting/failed/active) and maps them to the webhook-ingest queues, plus contract + client + hook.

items.feature: Background jobs & cron list — registry of scheduled jobs with schedule/last-run/status (reconciliation, child-address sweep, sanctions refresh, statement-link regen)
items.detail: FE renders JOB_ROWS (4 hardcoded consts: id/name/schedule/last/status/health). No endpoint enumerates cron/background jobs with their schedules and last-run outcomes. Real cron behaviour is scattered (settlement-reconciliation.service, wallet reconcile is admin-triggered not cron by default, child-address sweep, sanctions) but there is no job-registry read model or GET /admin/ops/jobs endpoint, DTO, client, or hook. Building it needs a jobs registry (name→schedule→last run/status, likely a new JobRun read model or a scheduler introspection) surfaced via a new contract + service + client + hook.

items.feature: Run a background job now (Run now → reason → step-up → engine-action, engine-brokered)
items.detail: FE 'Run now' opens the shared ReasonModal→StepUpModal→EngineActionModal flow and executeRun just pushes a toast + closes — no network. There is no generic POST /admin/ops/jobs/:id/run endpoint. Two SPECIFIC job triggers DO exist and are the model to follow: admin-wallets.controller POST /admin/wallets/backfill-networks (enqueues BackfillRun via BullMQ, 202 + runId, @RequirePermission execute) and POST /admin/wallets/reconcile (WalletReconciliationService, idempotent, engine-brokered, no auto-debit). Building 'Run now' means a per-job dispatch endpoint that maps the ops-job id to its enqueue path, permission-gated + step-up, returning a run handle — reusing the BackfillRun/reconcile pattern. Not just-wire because there is no unified job-run endpoint and no client/hook.

items.feature: Service health (per-transactable-service success rate) — already-built read model NOT surfaced on the Ops screen
items.detail: AdminMetricsService.serviceHealth (ServiceHealthMetricsSchema: per service {total, completed, failed, successRate}) is fully built, wired into GET /admin/metrics/dashboard, has a contract, a client (metrics.getDashboardMetrics), and a hook (useDashboardMetrics), and already renders on the operational-metrics dashboard (per recent commit 031b677). The Ops screen's header promises 'error rates' but its tiles show PROVIDER health, not this per-service success-rate block — so this existing signal is simply not surfaced on /ops. Small effort to add a service-error-rate strip to OpsPage using the existing hook (intentional-ish omission — the data lives on the metrics dashboard today; decide whether Ops should duplicate it).

items.feature: Wallet backfill run — enqueue + poll status (existing engine-brokered job) not surfaced as an Ops job
items.detail: admin-wallets.controller POST /admin/wallets/backfill-networks (→ EnqueueBackfillResponse {runId}, 202) and GET /admin/wallets/backfill-runs/:id (→ BackfillRunStatusDto with scanned/perNetwork/failures/timestamps) are fully built + permission-gated, and BackfillRun is a real Prisma model. The Ops screen invents its own JOB_ROWS list and never surfaces this real, pollable job. No web-admin lib/api client or hook wraps these routes yet, so surfacing it is FE work (add a client fn + hook + a real job row / progress card). Good candidate to be the first real entry in the ops job registry.
